ideas: What happened and how you heard about it
Why it affected you so strongly
What it made you think about afterwards

phrases.meaning: trying to finish before it's too late

model: A news story that's really stayed with me is the rescue of the boys' football team from a cave in Thailand in 2018. Twelve boys and their coach were trapped deep inside a flooded cave for more than two weeks. It hit the headlines all over the world, and I remember following the story every evening after work. Like millions of people, I was glued to the screen during the rescue, because it was a real race against time. The monsoon rains were coming, and the oxygen levels inside the cave were dropping. Divers from lots of different countries came to help, and sadly one of them, a former Thai navy diver, died during the operation. I remember holding my breath when the news said the first boys had been brought out. In the end, against all odds, all thirteen were rescued. It seems to me that it affected people so strongly because it was a rare story where the whole world wanted the same outcome. Most news tends to divide people, but this one brought everyone together. I'd say it restored my faith in humanity, at least to some extent, because strangers risked their lives for children they'd never met. Arguably, it also showed how much can be achieved through cooperation. Whenever I feel negative about the news, I still think about that rescue.
